### what_to_do_first.details[1]
Sentence: Because the Health Care Act sets no maximum time for a cancer suspicion, the team recommends reporting referral-to-treatment access times and handover alerts using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 guidance definitions for 16 cancers, while the roadmap plans target times by 2026–2028 and the Filha diagnostics recommendation is due before the 2030 evaluation.

Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers. | notes: the team's own DRAFT recommendation, not yet reviewed by mentors; not evidence. ### what_to_do_first.details[2]
Sentence: Supported by mentor insight that a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating in specialist care and because local referral instructions vary, the team recommends a standard referral template, referring persistent symptoms after a normal X-ray to a pulmonologist, and naming a diagnostic contact, while the roadmap plans standardised referral criteria and care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028.
Cited claims:
  [rec:2] status=recommendation (ours) | source: docs/recommendations.md, §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact | Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis. | notes: the team's own DRAFT recommendation, not yet reviewed by mentors; not evidence. flags.sentence: County treatment shares in the public report are crude (not adjusted for age or stage) because stage at diagnosis is missing for ~48% of new patients nationally, and age-adjusted figures digitised from Kuva 16 (precision ±0.5 percentage points) provide national reference lines here only for curative treatment (26.7% for men; 26.9% for women).
flags.problem: The cited claims state that missing stage at diagnosis (~48%) prevents stage adjustment of curative shares, not that it is the reason county treatment shares are not age-adjusted.

flags.sentence: Public report data do not measure symptom onset or referrals, do not include outpatient primary care visits or mention occupational health, capture imaging only indirectly as the diagnostic basis in approximately 20% of cases, and show whether a specialist visit (93.6%) or treatment occurred within 12 months without start dates.
flags.problem: According to the cited quote q:5eb155decc, approximately 20% refers to clinical examination alone (such as imaging), rather than imaging specifically.
